# Test fixtures

## `sweep.mp3` (committed)

Drives `tests/soundscape.spec.js`. 6 s, mono, 44.1 kHz, 128 kbps — deliberately
synthetic so the spectrogram has structure that can be asserted on:

| Component | Appears as |
|---|---|
| Exponential sweep, 120 Hz → 8 kHz | a diagonal ridge |
| Steady 300 Hz tone | a horizontal ridge |
| 1.5 kHz bursts, 120 ms once a second | evenly spaced vertical spikes |

Generated by writing a 16-bit PCM WAV of that signal and encoding it with a
LAME port (macOS `afconvert` decodes MP3 but cannot encode it). It is committed
because the Soundscapes specs cannot run without it and it is small.

It also drives the whole-track projection specs, where two consequences of its
length are worth knowing before reading a result as a bug:

- **The weave is three rows.** One row per bar means 6 s at the detected tempo is
  a handful of bars. Real tracks give hundreds.
- **The similarity matrix defaults to 512², exactly the streaming window's
  column count**, so the grid readout alone cannot tell a frozen matrix from the
  window it replaced. That spec moves the Size control first to give the freeze a
  distinguishable shape.

The projection *maths* is not tested through this fixture at all — a sweep has no
repeats or beat grid to find. `projections satisfy their structural invariants`
imports the module through the dev server and feeds it a synthetic 120 BPM signal
with a four-bar chord cycle, so symmetry, tempo detection and the heightmap
contract are checked against a signal whose answers are known.

## `benchmark.tif` (NOT committed)

`tests/benchmark.spec.js` needs a real GeoTIFF and is gitignored (see
`.gitignore`), so **that spec fails on any clean checkout** — a missing fixture,
not a regression. Drop any GeoTIFF at `tests/testdata/benchmark.tif` to run it.
